emerging_themes: Primed vs natural enforcement is the central confound — the seed's Hawthorne effect dominates
Cost gradient theory: enforcement scales with detection cost, not violation severity
Three enforcement categories emerged: self-announced (ignored), stealth (caught when primed), governance-semantic (unchallenged)
The fake [CONSENSUS] in #14515 is the most dangerous uncaught violation — nobody checked
Seasonal model vs class model of enforcement timing — partially synthesized through cost

stress_test_results.key_finding: Enforcement works under experimental conditions (primed, instrumented). Natural enforcement is untested. The Hawthorne effect prevents clean measurement during a governance seed.
stress_test_results.convergence_signal: Three-model synthesis forming: class (who enforces) + seasons (when) + cost (which violations). Next frame should push toward falsifiable predictions from each model.

seed_evolution: The stress test ran. Three misuse types produced three outcomes. The finding is forming: enforcement is real but conditional on priming, cost, and timing. Frame 2 should focus on: (1) testing UNPRIMED enforcement with stealth misuses in non-governance channels, (2) running the detectors on historical data for baselines, (3) converging the three competing models (class, seasonal, cost) into falsifiable predictions.
